definition: Cash and cash equivalents held by the company.
Short-term investments that can be quickly converted to cash.
Amounts owed to the company by customers for goods/services delivered.
Value of goods held for sale or production.
gaap_ifrs_variance: IFRS prohibits LIFO; US GAAP permits LIFO. Inventory write-down reversal rules also differ.

definition: Expenses paid in advance not yet consumed.
Assets expected to be realized, sold, or consumed in the normal operating cycle, held for trading, expected to be realized within twelve months, or qualifying as cash/cash equivalents.
Property, plant and equipment, net of accumulated depreciation and impairment.
gaap_ifrs_variance: IFRS permits either a cost model or revaluation model after recognition; US GAAP generally uses historical cost less depreciation and impairment.

definition: Premium paid over fair value in acquisitions.
Identifiable non-physical assets such as patents, trademarks, licenses and customer relationships, excluding goodwill.
Investments not expected to be liquidated within a year.
Sum of all assets owned by the company.
Amounts owed by the company to suppliers.
Short-term borrowings due within one year, excluding the current portion of long-term debt in this normalized ontology.
Expenses incurred but not yet paid.
Current portion of long-term borrowings contractually due within one year.

Obligations expected to be settled in the normal operating cycle, held for trading, due within twelve months, or for which the company lacks an unconditional right to defer settlement beyond that period.
Non-current portion of interest-bearing debt due beyond one year, excluding amounts classified as current.
Total interest-bearing debt: short-term borrowings plus the current portion of long-term debt plus non-current long-term debt.
Taxes owed in future periods due to timing differences.
Future pension payment obligations to employees.
Sum of all obligations owed by the company.
Par value of shares issued to shareholders.
Cumulative net income retained rather than distributed as dividends.
Amount received from shareholders above par value.
Value of shares repurchased by the company.
Shareholders' residual claim on assets after liabilities.
Standardized invested-capital proxy: shareholder equity plus total interest-bearing debt minus cash and marketable securities.
Number of common shares outstanding at the reporting date.
Fully diluted shares outstanding at the reporting date, when such a point-in-time measure is reported.
Weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the reporting period for basic EPS.

source_line_item: Weighted Average Common Shares Outstanding - Basic

definition: Weighted-average number of shares used for diluted EPS after including applicable dilutive potential common shares.

source_line_item: Weighted Average Common Shares Outstanding - Diluted

definition: Total value of goods/services sold in a period, before expenses.
Sales made on credit during the period, net of returns, allowances and related adjustments.
Direct costs attributable to producing goods/services sold.
Selling, general and administrative expenses.
Research and development expenses.
gaap_ifrs_variance: IFRS capitalizes qualifying development costs once specified criteria are met; US GAAP generally expenses research and development as incurred, subject to specific exceptions.

definition: Depreciation and amortization expense for the period.
Cost of borrowing for the period.
Income tax expense for the period.
Income before income tax expense for the reporting period.
Effective income tax rate for the period, calculated as income tax expense divided by pretax income.
Bottom-line profit after all expenses and taxes.
Cash generated from core business operations.
gaap_ifrs_variance: Classification of interest and dividend cash flows can differ between IFRS and US GAAP, affecting subtotals.

definition: Cash used in or generated from investing activities.
gaap_ifrs_variance: Classification of interest and dividend cash flows can differ between IFRS and US GAAP, affecting subtotals.

definition: Cash used in or generated from financing activities.
gaap_ifrs_variance: Classification of interest and dividend cash flows can differ between IFRS and US GAAP, affecting subtotals.

definition: Positive-magnitude cash outflow for purchases of long-term productive assets during the period.
Positive-magnitude cash outflow paid to shareholders as dividends during the period.
Positive-magnitude cash outflow used to repurchase company shares during the period.
Short-term liquidity buffer: current assets minus current liabilities.
Total assets minus goodwill, intangibles, and total liabilities.
Revenue minus cost of goods sold.
Total operating expenses as reported by the company. Prefer the reported total because expense components such as D&A may be embedded in COGS, SG&A or R&D.
Profit from operations as reported by the company, before non-operating items, interest and income taxes.
Standardized NOPAT approximation: operating income after applying the period effective tax rate.
Standardized EBITDA proxy calculated as reported operating income plus depreciation and amortization. It may differ from company-reported adjusted EBITDA.
Basic earnings per share as reported for the period.
Diluted earnings per share as reported for the period after applicable dilution adjustments.
Cash generated from operations after capital expenditures.
Ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets.
Ability to cover current liabilities with the most liquid current assets, excluding inventory and prepaid items.
Ability to cover current liabilities using cash, cash equivalents and highly liquid marketable securities.
Leverage measured as total debt relative to shareholder equity.
Proportion of total assets financed by debt.
Ability to cover interest expense with operating income.
Gross profit as a percentage of revenue.
Operating income as a percentage of revenue.
Net income as a percentage of revenue.
Net income generated per unit of shareholder equity.
Net income generated per unit of total assets.
Standardized return on invested capital: NOPAT divided by average invested capital.
Revenue generated per unit of total assets.
How many times inventory is sold and replaced over a period.
Net credit sales generated per unit of average accounts receivable.
Average number of days required to collect receivables generated from credit sales.
